items.title: For a separable algebraic extension the multiplication map is a localisation of the square
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a separable algebraic extension the multiplication map on the square of the extension is obtained by inverting a multiplicative subset (statement lines 10437-10443). The proof handles the finite separable case through a primitive element and its separable minimal polynomial, then passes to the general case by writing the extension as a filtered colimit of finite separable subextensions and observing that every element of the kernel is killed at a finite stage, so that exactness of localisation finishes (proof lines 10445-10472). The reduction to finitely generated subextensions is the step that carries the general case. H2.
